technical_decisions.decision: Bounded new packaging-smoke implementation (option B), reusing the release-artifacts.yml roundtrip sequence as an EXTRACT_AND_GENERALIZE donor. release-artifacts.yml is left untouched.
technical_decisions.evidence: The release smoke is insufficient for #490 for five independently verified reasons: (1) it is not a required per-PR context - it triggers on push to main/release/** plus a pull_request paths filter of only pyproject.toml and its own file, so a PR touching ci.yml never runs it, and it is not one of the ruleset required contexts (quality, security, infrastructure); (2) it probes only commander-lab while pyproject.toml declares two console scripts, leaving commander-lab-optimizer unprobed; (3) it emits no machine-readable SHA/TREE/digest-bound evidence; (4) it installs the wheel with default unpinned index resolution of the dependency closure; (5) it has no adversarial controls and nothing proves the import came from the installation rather than a source tree.
technical_decisions.rejected_alternative: Option A (minimal integration of the existing release smoke into required CI evidence) - rejected because items 1-5 above are each independently disqualifying.

technical_decisions.decision: Add the packaging smoke as two new steps inside the existing required `quality` job, after `Build wheel`, rather than as a new job or a new workflow.
technical_decisions.evidence: scripts/verify_required_check_definitions.py defines REQUIRED_CONTEXTS['quality'] with a `package_wheel` category matching '^\s*python\s+-m\s+pip\s+wheel', so that step is preserved byte-identically. Placing the smoke inside `quality` makes a broken wheel/entrypoint/evidence actually fail the gate, which is issue #490's completion criterion. A new job would be non-required by default and therefore would not gate.
technical_decisions.rejected_alternative: A separate packaging-smoke job or workflow - rejected because it would not be a required context, so the gate would be advisory.

technical_decisions.decision: Provision the isolated environment's dependency closure from the project's own hash-pinned requirements/lock.txt using `pip install --require-hashes`, then install the project itself with `pip install --no-index --no-deps --force-reinstall <exact wheel path>`, and verify the wheel's own non-extra Requires-Dist entries are satisfied from inside the isolated env.
technical_decisions.evidence: Measured on Python 3.14.4: hash-pinned lock install into a fresh venv succeeds in ~17 s. `pip download --require-hashes -r requirements/lock.txt` was rejected as the provisioning mechanism because the lock's transitive `pip-api` -> `pip` edge is not `==`-pinned, so a download-based wheelhouse cannot be built without inventing a new pin authority. The `--no-index --no-deps` project install plus an explicit in-venv Requires-Dist satisfaction check is deterministic, uses no new authority surface, and still proves the wheel's own dependency metadata is satisfiable from a fixed hash-pinned artifact set.
technical_decisions.rejected_alternative: A download-based wheelhouse; consuming the runner's already-installed editable project or its ambient site-packages; default index resolution at install time.

technical_decisions.decision: Prove install provenance from the installed distribution's own pip `direct_url.json`: require `archive_info`, reject `dir_info`, require the basename to equal the wheel filename, and require the recorded SHA-256 to equal the digest bound before installing. Reject `__editable__*` / `*.egg-link` markers.
technical_decisions.evidence: Verified locally: `pip install --no-index --no-deps <wheel>` writes direct_url.json = {"archive_info": {"hash": "sha256=...", "hashes": {"sha256": "..."}}, "url": "file:///.../commander_playtest_lab-1.25.0-py3-none-any.whl"}, which binds the installed distribution to the exact artifact digest.

technical_decisions.decision: Run the import probe with the venv interpreter under `-I` (implies -E -P -s), with PYTHONPATH and PYTHONHOME scrubbed from the child environment and cwd outside the repository; require the imported module file to resolve under the venv's own purelib and require that no repository path appears on the probe's sys.path.
technical_decisions.evidence: Verified: an ambient PYTHONPATH pointed at <repo>/src does not change the outcome - the positive control still PASSes and still attests installed_import.resolved_in_isolated_environment=true. The strongest control is a decoy wheel that installs cleanly, declares the current version and makes `import commander_lab` genuinely succeed via a .pth pointing at src/; the smoke rejects it with a provenance failure.

Measured additive cost of the packaging smoke with a warm pip cache: venv creation ~1.7 s, hash-pinned lock install ~16.7 s, wheel install ~0.8 s - about 19 s total, plus two sub-second CLI probes. The job already installs the same lock and configures `cache: pip`, so the additive cost stays far inside the existing budget and no budget had to be widened.

technical_decisions.decision: Bind evidence to the digest of the wheel built in that run and never assume a precomputed wheel digest.
technical_decisions.evidence: Two builds of the identical source produced digests 4d721b05... and 060610754..., because setuptools wheels are not byte-reproducible by default. Cross-run digest comparison would require a reproducible-build change that is out of B9 scope; it is recorded as a residual risk instead of being claimed.

technical_decisions.decision: Eliminate the three implicit candidates[0] picks via an explicit _only() helper that fails closed on an ambiguous set, instead of adding a reviewed BASELINE entry to tests/unit/test_first_option_ratchet.py.
technical_decisions.evidence: The ratchet's own contract permits either an explicit choice or a reviewed baseline entry. Elimination was chosen because it is strictly stronger: it also closes a real latent defect in which a venv containing two lib/python*/site-packages trees would previously have silently used whichever sorted first, which would have made the evidence non-reproducible. The ratchet now reports zero occurrences for scripts/verify_packaging_smoke.py and no BASELINE entry was added, so the gate was not weakened.
technical_decisions.rejected_alternative: Adding a reviewed BASELINE entry, which would have permitted the latent first-pick ambiguity to remain in a fail-closed isolation tool.
